meta.title: Innovative MXene/SilMA-Based Conductive Bioink for Three Dimensional Bioprinting of Neural Stem Cell Spheroids in Neural Tissue Engineering.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A conductive silk-methacrylate/pectin bioink with MXene nanosheets was used to print rat neural stem cell spheroids and stimulate them electrically. The printed conduit also supported sciatic nerve regeneration in rats.

formulations.review_notes: Viability is given as a threshold ('above 80%'). The text gives the pressure range in mm/min (a unit error), so pressure is left null.
formulations.name: 20% SilMA + pectin + MXene-SP (conductive)
formulations.composition_detail: 20% SilMA series with pectin and SP-modified MXene
formulations.key_outcome: All MXene groups stayed above 80% viability by day 5; softer gels promoted neuronal differentiation.

evidence.quote: we selected the 20% SilMA series with SP-modified MXene
all groups exhibited cell viability above 80% by day 5
Extrusion parameters were configured in Ultimaker Cura to match the nozzle size (22g, 0.413 mm)
Primary cortical NSCs were isolated from embryonic day 16 (ED16) Wistar rat cortices
